meta.title: Shenzhou-23 reentry
meta.subtitle: Dongfeng landing site · forecast touchdown 21:12 UTC
about: Forecast of the Shenzhou-23 return, made 11 Nov 2026: the China Space Station orbit from CelesTrak supplemental elements (CMSA ephemeris) after the 13 November reboost, and the deorbit burn and bank magnitude reconstructed for Shenzhou-20. Not an official schedule: the landing day, the pass and the burn are CMSA's to choose.
WGS-84 geometry · JPL DE440s sunlight · NRLMSIS 2.1 column at 41.654 N 100.754 E.
notes: Forecast, not official ephemeris. One SGP4 set fitted to the 18 CelesTrak supplemental GP segments of the CSS (NORAD 48274, from the CMSA ephemeris) after the reboost of 13 Nov 2026: 2026-11-13T12:00 to 2026-11-18T00:00 UTC, fit RMS 0.6 km along track; propagated 12.1 days with its fitted B*.

The descent is the Shenzhou-20 reconstruction moved onto this pass: a 3-DOF simulation (WGS-84, J2, rotating Earth, NRLMSIS 2.1 column) with the same burn (138.8 m/s in 160 s) and bank magnitude (47°). The ignition time and the bank reversal are solved so that the capsule reaches the Dongfeng aim point; the landing time is an output.

Timing: a drag error of ±30 % over the days of propagation moves the pass by ±45 s; a further station manoeuvre, a different burn or entry angle, or a different pass would move it more. The free-flying spacecraft also leaves the station orbit by a few km after undocking, which is not modeled.
The T0 slider moves the Sun only: the Earth-fixed track stays. Its presets are the forecast time and the drag-error bounds.
Plasma blackout is marked between the published 80 km and 40 km heights; the orange glow illustrates the self-luminous trail and is not a brightness model.
Winds, the retro-rocket pulse, attitude dynamics and the real guidance law are not modeled; the single bank reversal is a proxy for the roll-modulated entry guidance.
